2278.text: The type of epithelial cells which line the inner surface of Fallopian tubes, bronchioles and small bronchi are known as
2278.sol: Ciliated epithelium is a region of epithelium consisting of columnar or cuboidal cells bearing hairlike appendages that are capable of beating rapidly. Ciliated epithelium performs the functions of moving particles of fluids over the epithelial surface. Cuboidal ciliated epithelium occurs in certain parts of uriniferous tubules whereas columnar ciliated epithelium occurs in fallopian tubules, nasal passages, bronchioles, small bronchi and buccopharyngeal cavity of frog. It often occurs in the vicinity of mucus secreting goblet cells.

7039.subject: Mathematics
7039.text: If the equation of a curve $C$ is transformed to $9x^{2} + 25y^{2} = 225$ by the rotation of the coordinate axes about the origin through an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ in the positive direction then the equation of the curve $C$, before the transformation is
7039.sol:
The original and new coordinates are,

$x = xcos\dfrac{\pi}{4} - ysin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{x}{2} - \dfrac{y}{2}$

$y = xsin\dfrac{\pi}{4} + ycos\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{y}{2}$

The equation of the curve is,

$9x^{2} + 25y^{2} = 225$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right)^{2} + 25\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right)^{2} = 225$

After simplification,

$9x^{2} + 9y^{2} + 18xy + 25x^{2} + 25y^{2} - 50xy = 450$

$⇒ 34x^{2} + 34y^{2} - 32xy = 450$

$⇒ 17x^{2} + 17y^{2} - 16xy = 225$

7971.subject: Mathematics
7971.text: If the system of simultaneous linear equations \(x+y+z=a, x-y+b z=2\), \(2 x+3 y-z=1\) has infinitely many solutions, then \(b-5 a=\)
7971.sol:
Given that system of linear equations
\(\begin{aligned}
x+y+z & =a \quad \ldots (i)\\
x-y+b z & =2 \quad \ldots (ii) \\
2 x+3 y-z & =1 \quad \ldots (iii)
\end{aligned}\)
has infinitely many solutions,
\(\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad\left[\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 1 & 1 \\
1 & -1 & b \\
2 & 3 & -1
\end{array}\right]=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 1(1-3 b)-1(-1-2 b)+1(3+2=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 1-3 b+1+2 b+5=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \\
& -b=-7 \\
& \Rightarrow \\
& b=7
\end{aligned}\)
Adding Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get
\(\quad \begin{aligned}
2 x+8 z & =a+2 \\
\Rightarrow x+4 z & =\frac{a+2}{2}  \quad \ldots (iv)
\end{aligned}\)
Multiply Eq. (i) by 3 then subtract Eq. (iii) from it,
\(\begin{aligned}
3 x+3 y+3 z & =3 a \\
-2 x \pm 3 y \mp z & =-1 \\
\hline x+4 z & =3 a-1 \quad \ldots (v)
\end{aligned}\)
By Eqs. (iv) and (v), we get
\($\begin{array}{rlrl} 
& & \frac{a+2}{2} & =3 a-1 \\
\Rightarrow & & a+2 & =6 a-2 \\
\Rightarrow & 6 a-a & =4 \\
\Rightarrow & & 5 a & =4 \\
\therefore & b-5 a & =7-4=3
\end{array}$

12759.sol:
In $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}$, given
$\begin{aligned}
& x=\tan \left(\frac{B-C}{2}\right) \tan \frac{A}{2} \\
& y=\tan \left(\frac{C-A}{2}\right) \tan \frac{B}{2}
\end{aligned}$ and $y=\tan \left(\frac{A-B}{2}\right) \tan \frac{C}{2}$
Since, $\tan \left(\frac{B-C}{2}\right)=\frac{b-c}{b+c} \tan \frac{A}{2}\Rightarrow \quad x=\frac{b-c}{b+c}$
Similarly, $y=\frac{c-a}{c+c}$ and $z=\frac{a-b}{a+b}$
Now, by componendo and dividendo
$\frac{1+x}{1-x}=\frac{b+c+b-c}{b+c-b+c}=\frac{b}{c}$
Similarly, $\frac{1+y}{1-y}=\frac{c}{a}$ and $\frac{1+z}{1-z}=\frac{a}{b}\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \quad\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right)\left(\frac{1+y}{1-y}\right)\left(\frac{1+z}{1-z}\right)=\frac{b}{c} \times \frac{c}{a} \times \frac{a}{b}=1 \\
\Rightarrow & (1+x)(1+y)(1+z) \\
= & (1-x)(1-y)(1-z) \\
\Rightarrow & 1+x+y+z+x y+y z+z x+x y z \\
= & 1-(x+y+z)+x y+y z+z x-x y z \\
\Rightarrow & x+y+z=-x y z
\end{aligned}$

15324.sol: By parallelogram law of vector addition, angle made by resultant with $\mathbf{P}$ is given by; $\tan \alpha=\frac{Q \sin \theta}{P+Q \cos \theta}$ Here $\alpha=90^{{}^{\circ}}$ so ; $\tan 90^{{}^{\circ}}=\infty=\frac{Q \sin \theta}{P+Q \cos \theta}\Rightarrow \quad P+Q \cos \theta=0$ or $Q \cos \theta=-P$ Now, magnitude of resultant, $R=\sqrt{P^2+Q^2+2 P Q \cos \theta}$ Here, we have $R=2 P$ and $Q \cos \theta=-P$ and $Q=10 \mathrm{ m}$ So, $\quad 2 P=\sqrt{P^2+100-2 P^2}\Rightarrow \quad 4 P^2=100-P^2 \Rightarrow 5 P^2=100$ or $\quad P=\sqrt{20}=2 \sqrt{5} \mathrm{ m}$ Magnitude of $P$ is $2 \sqrt{5} \mathrm{ m}$

& \frac{\rho_1}{\rho_2}=1 \\

By using de-Broglie wavelength, \lambda=$\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m e V}}$ where, $h$ is Planck's constant $=6.63 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{ J}-\mathrm{s}$, $m$ is mass of electron,
$e$ is charge of electron
and $V$ is applied voltage. $\begin{aligned}
\therefore \quad$ V & =$\frac{h^2}{2 m e \lambda^2}$\\
& =$\frac{\left(6.63 \times 10^{-34}\right)^2}{2 \times 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times\left(0.5 \times 10^{-10}\right)^2}$\\
& =602 $\mathrm{ V}
\end{aligned}$

17447.text: Which one of the following arrangements represents the correct order of electron gain enthalpy (with negative sign) of the given atomic species?
17447.sol: The amount of energy released when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom to produce a monovalent anion is called electron gain enthalpy. Electron affinity value generally increase on moving from left to right in a period however there are exceptions of this rule in the case of those atoms which have stable configuration. These atoms resist the addition of extra electron, therefore the low value of electron affinity $\underset{-1.48}{\mathrm{O}}< \underset{-2.0}{\mathrm{ S}}< \underset{-3.6}{\mathrm{ F}}< \underset{-3.8}{\mathrm{Cl}}$ On the other hand $\mathrm{Cl}$, because of its comparatively bigger size than $\mathrm{F}$, allow the addition of an extra electron more easily.

$P\left(A\right) = \dfrac{C2 5}{C3 8}$ (number less than $6$ is $5$)

$P\left(B\right) = \dfrac{C2 5}{C3 8}$ (number greater than $3$ is $5$)

$P\left(A \cap B\right) = \dfrac{C1 2}{C3 8}$

$∴$ Required probability

$= P\left(B / A\right) = \dfrac{P\left(A \cap B\right)}{P\left(A\right)} = \dfrac{C1 2}{C2 5} = \dfrac{2}{10} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

19429.text: Transverse waves of the same frequency are generated in two steel wires $A$ and $B$. The diameter of $A$ is twice that of $B$ and the tension in $A$ is half that in $B$. The ratio of the velocities of the waves in $A$ and $B$ is
19429.sol: The velocity of transverse waves is given by $v=\sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}$ where, $T=$ Tension and $m=$ mass per unit length of the wire. If $r$ is the radius of the wire and $\rho$ its density then, $m=\pi r^2 \rho\therefore \quad v=\sqrt{\frac{T}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{T}{\pi r^2 \rho}}\therefore \quad v_A=\frac{\sqrt{T_A}}{r_A \sqrt{\pi \rho}}$ and $\quad v_B=\frac{\sqrt{T_B}}{r_B \sqrt{\pi \rho}}$ Now, $\quad \frac{v_A}{v_B}=\sqrt{\frac{T_A}{T_B}} \cdot \frac{r_B}{r_A}\because \quad r_A=2 r_B$ and $T_A=\frac{1}{2} T_B$ Hence, $\quad \frac{v_A}{v_B}=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}$

20786.subject: Chemistry
20786.text:
Given below are 4 subatomic particles travelling with the same velocity "v". Which of them will have the shortest wavelength?
$[A]=\text{ Proton }[B]=\text{ Neutron. }[C]=\text{ Alpha particle. }[D]=$$\text{ Electron. }$
20786.sol:
According to the de Broglie hypothesis, the wavelength $\lambda$ of a particle moving with velocity $v$ is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant and $m$ is the mass of the particle.

Since $h$ and $v$ are constant for all particles, the wavelength $\lambda$ is inversely proportional to the mass $m$ of the particle, i.e., $\lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{m}$.

To find the shortest wavelength, we must identify the particle with the largest mass among the given options:
Mass of electron ($m_e$) $\approx 9.1 \times 10^{-31}$ kg.
Mass of proton ($m_p$) $\approx 1.67 \times 10^{-27}$ kg.
Mass of neutron ($m_n$) $\approx 1.675 \times 10^{-27}$ kg.
Mass of alpha particle ($m_{\alpha}$) $\approx 4 \times m_p \approx 6.68 \times 10^{-27}$ kg.

Comparing the masses, the alpha particle has the largest mass among the given particles. Therefore, the alpha particle will have the shortest de Broglie wavelength.

Answer: [C]

22062.subject: Mathematics
22062.text: In the set $\mathrm{W}$ of whole numbers an equivalence relation $\mathrm{R}$ is defined as follows $\mathrm{aRb}$ iff both $\mathrm{a} \mathrm{ b}$ leave the same reminder when divided by 5. The equivalence class of 1 is given by.
22062.sol:
The relation $R$ is defined on the set of whole numbers $W = \{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}$ such that $aRb$ if and only if $a \equiv b \pmod{5}$.

The equivalence class of an element $x$, denoted by $[x]$, is the set of all elements $y \in W$ such that $yRx$.

For $x = 1$, the equivalence class $[1]$ consists of all whole numbers $y$ such that $y \equiv 1 \pmod{5}$.

This means $y = 5k + 1$ for some non-negative integer $k$.

Substituting values for $k = 0, 1, 2, 3, \dots$:
For $k = 0$, $y = 5(0) + 1 = 1$.
For $k = 1$, $y = 5(1) + 1 = 6$.
For $k = 2$, $y = 5(2) + 1 = 11$.
For $k = 3$, $y = 5(3) + 1 = 16$.

Thus, the equivalence class of 1 is the set $\{1, 6, 11, 16, \dots\}$.

Answer: $\{1,6,11,16------\}$

22790.subject: Physics
22790.text: Uniform electric field of $5 \times 10^3\,NC^{-1}$ is maintained in the positive Y direction. Now a point charge of $2 \times 10^{-4}C$ at rest is released from the origin. The kinetic energy attained by the charge when it is 5 m from the origin is:
22790.sol:
The force experienced by the point charge in the uniform electric field is given by $F = qE$.

Since the charge is released from rest, it moves along the direction of the electric field (positive Y direction).

The work done by the electric field when the charge moves a distance $d$ is $W = Fd = qEd$.

By the work-energy theorem, the kinetic energy attained by the charge is equal to the work done on it by the electric field.

$K = qEd$

Substituting the given values:

$K = (2 \times 10^{-4}) \times (5 \times 10^3) \times 5$

$K = 10 \times 10^{-1} \times 5$

$K = 1 \times 5 = 5$ J.

Answer: $5$ J

22843.subject: Physics
22843.text: PQRS is square of side $1 \mathrm{ m}$. A charge of $100 \mu \mathrm{C}$ is placed at the centre of the square. Then the work done to take $3 \mu \mathrm{C}$ charge from the corner $\mathrm{P}$ to the corner $\mathrm{R}$.
22843.sol:
The electric potential $V$ at any point at a distance $r$ from a point charge $q$ is given by $V = \dfrac{kq}{r}$.

Let the charge at the centre of the square be $Q = 100 \mu \text{C} = 100 \times 10^{-6} \text{C}$.

The distance from the centre of a square of side $a = 1 \text{m}$ to any of its corners is $r = \dfrac{a}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \text{m}$.

Since the distance from the centre to corner P is $r_P = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \text{m}$ and the distance from the centre to corner R is $r_R = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \text{m}$, the potential at P and R are equal:

$V_P = \dfrac{kQ}{r_P} = \sqrt{2}kQ$

$V_R = \dfrac{kQ}{r_R} = \sqrt{2}kQ$

The work done $W$ in moving a charge $q_0 = 3 \mu \text{C}$ from P to R is given by $W = q_0(V_R - V_P)$.

Since $V_R = V_P$, the potential difference $V_R - V_P = 0$.

Therefore, $W = q_0 \times 0 = 0 \text{J}$.

Answer: Zero

24841.subject: Chemistry
24841.text: Treatment of buta-1,3-diyne with $\text{NaNH}_2$ ($2$ equivalents), followed by reaction with excess of $trans$-$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-Br}$ gives $\textbf{X}$ as the major product. The maximum number of carbon atoms that are collinear (in a straight line) in $\textbf{X}$ is ____.
24841.sol:
Buta-1,3-diyne ($HC \equiv C - C \equiv CH$) reacts with $2$ equivalents of $\text{NaNH}_2$ to undergo double deprotonation, forming the acetylide dianion:

$HC \equiv C - C \equiv CH + 2\text{NaNH}_2 \rightarrow \ ^\ominus C \equiv C - C \equiv C ^\ominus + 2\text{NH}_3$

This dianion acts as a strong nucleophile and undergoes an $S_N2$ reaction with the primary allylic halide, $trans$-$\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-Br}$ (excess ensures both sides react):

$^\ominus C \equiv C - C \equiv C ^\ominus + 2 \text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-Br} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2 - C \equiv C - C \equiv C - \text{CH}_2\text{-CH=CH-CH}_3$

In the major product $\textbf{X}$, the central diyne unit consists of four $sp$ hybridized carbon atoms. The geometry around $sp$ hybridized carbons is linear (bond angle $180^\circ$).

The two $sp^3$ hybridized $-\text{CH}_2-$ carbons attached directly to the $sp$ carbons also lie on this same linear axis. Thus, the sequence of collinear carbon atoms is:

$-\text{CH}_2 - C \equiv C - C \equiv C - \text{CH}_2-$

The carbon atoms beyond the $-\text{CH}_2-$ groups are attached at a tetrahedral angle ($\sim 109.5^\circ$) and are not collinear with the central axis.

Therefore, the maximum number of collinear carbon atoms in $\textbf{X}$ is $6$.

Answer: $6$

26156.subject: Physics
26156.text: A circular insulated copper wire loop is twisted to form two loops of area $A$ and $2A$ as shown in the figure. At the point of crossing the wires remain electrically insulated from each other. The entire loop lies in the plane (of the paper). A uniform magnetic field $\overset{\to}{B}$ points into the plane of the paper. At $t = 0$ , the loop starts rotating about the common diameter as axis with a constant angular velocity in the magnetic field. Which of the following options is/are correct?
options: The net emf induced due to both the loops is proportional to  $cos ⁡ \omegat$
The amplitude of the maximum net emf induced due to both the loops is equal to the amplitude of the maximum emf induced in the smaller loop alone
The rate of change of flux is maximum when plane of loop is perpendicular to the plane of paper
The emf induced in the loop is proportional to sum of areas of two loops
26156.sol:
When a conducting loop rotating in a magnetic field $B$has an angular velocity $\omega$, the flux through the loop of area $A$ at an angle $\theta = \omegat$, 

$ϕ = \left|B\right|\left|A\right|cos ⁡ \theta$

$= BAcos ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)$

The induced emf,

$ε = - \dfrac{dϕ}{dt} = BA\omegasin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)$

So,  $εand\dfrac{dϕ}{dt} ∝ sin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)$

So, the emf is maximum when, $\omegat = \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2} .$

Since the emf in the smaller loop will act opposite to that of the larger loop,

${ε}_{Net} = {ε}_{2A} - {ε}_{A} = B\left(2A\right)\omegasin ⁡ \omegat - B\left(A\right)\omegasin ⁡ \left(\omegat\right)$

$= B\left(2A - A\right)\omegasin ⁡ \omegat = BA\omegasin ⁡ \omegat$

So, the amplitude of the maximum net emf is equal to $BA$ which is same as that in the smaller loop.

27185.subject: Chemistry
27185.text: The number of compounds from the following which can undergo reaction with Br$_2$/KOH (alcoholic) to give respective products and these respective products can also be obtained separately by Gabriel phthalimide reaction is :
27185.sol:
The reaction of an amide with $\text{Br}_2/\text{KOH}$ (alcoholic) is the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction. This reaction is specific to primary amides ($R-\text{CONH}_2$) and produces primary amines ($R-\text{NH}_2$) with one less carbon atom.

Among the given compounds, the primary amides are:
1. Benzamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONH}_2$)
2. 2-Phenylacetamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$)
3. Acetamide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2$)
4. Cyclohexanecarboxamide ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{CONH}_2$)

The other two compounds (N-ethylcyclohexanecarboxamide and N-methylpivalamide) are secondary amides and do not undergo this reaction.

The primary amines formed from the degradation of the four primary amides are:
1. Aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$)
2. Benzylamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$)
3. Methylamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$)
4. Cyclohexylamine ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{11}\text{NH}_2$)

The Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of aliphatic primary amines. It cannot be used to prepare aromatic primary amines (like aniline) because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion.

Therefore, aniline cannot be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis. The remaining three amines (benzylamine, methylamine, and cyclohexylamine) are aliphatic primary amines and can be prepared by this method.

Thus, there are $3$ compounds that satisfy both conditions.

Answer: $3$

30267.sol:
(i) Fittig reaction: Aryl halides give analogous compounds when treated with sodium in dry ether, in which two aryl groups are joined together. It is called Fittig reaction.

(ii) Wurtz-Fittig reaction: A mixture of an alkyl halide and aryl halide gives an alkylarene when treated with sodium in dry ether and is called Wurtz-Fittig reaction.

(iii) Finkelstein reaction: Alkyl iodides are often prepared by the reaction of alkyl chlorides/ bromides with NaI in dry acetone. This reaction is known as Finkelstein reaction.

(iv) Sandmeyer reaction: When a primary aromatic amine, dissolved or suspended in cold aqueous mineral acid, is treated with sodium nitrite, a diazonium salt is formed. Mixing the solution of freshly prepared diazonium salt with cuprous chloride or cuprous bromide results in the replacement of the diazonium group by –Cl or –Br

33707.text: The equation of the circle described on the chord $3x ⁡ + y ⁡ + 5 = 0$ of the circle $x{⁡}^{2} + y{⁡}^{2} = 16$ as the diameter is
33707.sol:
We know that the equation of the family of circle passing through the point of intersection of a circle $S = 0$ and a line $L = 0$ is $S + \lambdaL = 0 .$

Hence, the family of circle passing through points of intersection of given circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 16 = 0$ and chord $3x + y + 5 = 0$ is $( {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 16 ) + \lambda\left(3x + y + 5\right) = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 3\lambdax + \lambday + 5\lambda - 16 = 0$

We know that, the centre of a circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$ is $\left(- g, - f\right)$

Hence, centre of the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 3\lambdax + \lambday + 5\lambda - 16 = 0$ is $\left(- \dfrac{3\lambda}{2}, - \dfrac{\lambda}{2}\right)$ and since, for this circle $AB$ is diameter, thus $\left(\dfrac{- 3\lambda}{2}, \dfrac{- \lambda}{2}\right)$ must lie on $AB$ i.e. $3x + y + 5 = 0$

$⇒ 3\left(- \dfrac{3\lambda}{2}\right) + \left(- \dfrac{\lambda}{2}\right) + 5 = 0$

$⇒ - \dfrac{9\lambda}{2} - \dfrac{\lambda}{2} + 5 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = 1 .$

Therefore, the equation of the required circle is ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 3 \times 1 \times x + 1 \times y + 5 \times 1 - 16 = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} + 3x + y - 11 = 0 .$

34436.subject: Mathematics
34436.text:
Consider the system of linear equations in $x, y, z$:
$x + 2y + tz = 0$,
$6x + y + 5tz = 0$,
$3x + t^2 y + f(t) z = 0$,
where $f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a differentiable function. If this system has infinitely many solutions for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, then $f$
34436.sol:
For a homogeneous system of linear equations to have infinitely many solutions, the determinant of its coefficient matrix must be zero.

The coefficient matrix is:
$\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & t \\ 6 & 1 & 5t \\ 3 & t^2 & f(t) \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding the determinant along the first row, we get:
$\Delta = 1(1 \cdot f(t) - 5t \cdot t^2) - 2(6 \cdot f(t) - 3 \cdot 5t) + t(6 \cdot t^2 - 3 \cdot 1)$

$\Delta = f(t) - 5t^3 - 12f(t) + 30t + 6t^3 - 3t$

$\Delta = -11f(t) + t^3 + 27t$

Since the system has infinitely many solutions for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, we must have $\Delta = 0$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

$-11f(t) + t^3 + 27t = 0$

$f(t) = \dfrac{t^3 + 27t}{11}$

To determine the nature of the function $f(t)$, we find its derivative with respect to $t$:

$f'(t) = \dfrac{3t^2 + 27}{11}$

Since $t^2 \ge 0$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, we have $3t^2 + 27 \ge 27 > 0$.

Therefore, $f'(t) > 0$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, which implies that $f(t)$ is a strictly increasing function on $\mathbb{R}$.

Answer: is strictly increasing on $\mathbb{R}$

35896.text: Let $p, q, r$ be three statements such that the truth value of $\left(p ∧ q\right) \to \left(~ q ∨ r\right) is $F$ . Then the truth values of $p, q, r$ are respectively :$
35896.sol:
Given that the truth value of $\left(p ∧ q\right) \to \left(~ q ∨ r\right)$ is $F$ .

For the above truth value to be possible, $\left(p ∧ q\right)$ should be TRUE and $\left(~ q ∨ r\right)$ should be FALSE.

$\left(p ∧ q\right)$ is TRUE when $p \text{ and } q$ both are TRUE.

$\left(~ q ∨ r\right)$ is FALSE when $q$ is TRUE and $r$ is FALSE.

So, the truth values of $p, q, r$ are $T, T, F$ respectively.

36335.subject: Mathematics
36335.text: The largest value of $n$, for which $40^{n}$ divides $60!$, is
36335.sol:
$40^n = 2^{3n} \times 5^n$. We need the highest power of $40$ dividing $60!$.
Power of $5$ in $60! = \lfloor 60/5 \rfloor + \lfloor 60/25 \rfloor = 12 + 2 = 14$.
Power of $2$ in $60! = \lfloor 60/2 \rfloor + \lfloor 60/4 \rfloor + \lfloor 60/8 \rfloor + \lfloor 60/16 \rfloor + \lfloor 60/32 \rfloor = 30 + 15 + 7 + 3 + 1 = 56$.
We need $n \leq 14$ and $3n \leq 56$ (i.e., $n \leq 18$).
The binding constraint is $n \leq 14$, so the largest value is $n = 14$.

36732.text: Let $E \text{ and } F$ be two independent events. The probability that $E \text{ and } F$ happen is $\dfrac{1}{12}$ and the probability that neither $E$ nor $F$ happens is $\dfrac{1}{2}$ , then a value of $\dfrac{P\left(E\right)}{P\left(F\right)}$ is:
36732.sol:
$P\left(E ∩ F\right) = P\left(E\right) . P\left(F\right) = \dfrac{1}{12}$

$⇒ xy = \dfrac{1}{12}$

$⇒ P\left(\overset{-}{E} ∩ \overset{-}{F}\right) = P\left(\overset{-}{E}\right) . P\left(\overset{-}{F}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \left(1 - P\left(E\right)\right)\left(1 - P\left(F\right)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 1 - x - y + xy = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 1 - x - y + \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 1 - x - y = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{5}{12}$

$⇒ x + y = \dfrac{7}{12}$

$⇒ x + \dfrac{1}{12x} = \dfrac{7}{12}$

$⇒ ⇒ \dfrac{12{x}^{2} + 1}{12x} = \dfrac{7}{12}$

$⇒ 12{x}^{2} - 7x + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 12{x}^{2} - 4x - 3x + 1 = 0$

$⇒ 4x\left(3x - 1\right) - 1\left(3x - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{3}, x = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{4}, y = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}}{\dfrac{1}{4}} \text{ and } \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4}}{\dfrac{1}{3}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{x}{y} = \dfrac{4}{3} \text{ and } \dfrac{3}{4}$

38233.text: The equation of the plane containing the line of intersection of $2x - 5y + z = 3; x + y + 4z = 5,$ and parallel to the plane, $x + 3y + 6z = 1,$ is
38233.sol:
Any plane containing the line of intersection of $2x - 5y + z = 3, x + y + 4z = 5$ will be of the form

$\left(2 x - 5 y + z - 3\right) + \lambda \left(x + y + 4 z - 5\right) = 0$

$\left(2 + \lambda\right) x - \left(5 - \lambda\right) y + \left(1 + 4 \lambda\right) z - \left(3 + 5 \lambda\right) = 0$

It is parallel to plane $x + 3 y + 6 z = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{2 + \lambda}{1} = \dfrac{\lambda - 5}{3} = \dfrac{1 + 4\lambda}{6} \ne \dfrac{\left(3 + 5\lambda\right)}{1}$

$\dfrac{2 + \lambda}{1} = \dfrac{\lambda - 5}{3} ⇒ 6 + 3 \lambda = \lambda - 5$

$2 \lambda = - 1 1$

$\lambda = \dfrac{- 1 1}{2}$

$∴$ Required plane is

$\left(2x - 5y + z - 3\right) + \dfrac{\left(- 11\right)}{2}\left(x + y + 4z - 5\right) = 0$

$2 \left(2 x - 5 y + z - 3\right) - 1 1 \left(x + y + 4 z - 5\right) = 0$

$4 x - 1 0 y + 2 z - 6 - 1 1 x - 1 1 y - 4 4 z + 5 5 = 0$

$- 7 x - 2 1 y - 4 2 z + 4 9 = 0$

$⇒ x + 3 y + 6 z - 7 = 0$

38526.subject: Mathematics
38526.text:
For any vector $\overset{\to}{a} = {a}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {a}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {a}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$, with $10\left|{a}_{i}\right| < 1, i = 1, 2, 3$, consider the following statements:
$\left(A\right)$ : $max\left\{\left|{a}_{1}\right|, \left|{a}_{2}\right|, \left|{a}_{3}\right|\right\} \le \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|$
$\left(B\right)$ : $| \overset{\to}{a} | \le 3max\left\{\left|{a}_{1}\right|, \left|{a}_{2}\right|, \left|{a}_{3}\right|\right\}$
38526.sol:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = {a}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {a}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {a}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$, with $10\left|{a}_{i}\right| < 1, i = 1, 2, 3$,

Let us assume that $\left|{a}_{1}\right| \le \left|{a}_{2}\right| \le \left|{a}_{3}\right|$

Now we know that,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}1\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}2\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2}$

And ${\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2} \le {\left|\overset{\to}{a}1\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}2\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2}$

So, combining both above equations we get,

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \ge {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| \ge \left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right| = \text{max}\left\{\left|\overset{\to}{a}1\right|, \left|\overset{\to}{a}2\right|\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|\right\}$

Hence, $\left(A\right)$ is true

Now again solving,

${\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}1\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}2\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2}$

And ${\left|\overset{\to}{a}1\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}2\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2} \le {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}1\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}2\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2} \le 3{\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \le 3{\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{\to}{a}\right| \le 3\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right| = \text{max}\left\{\left|\overset{\to}{a}1\right|, \left|\overset{\to}{a}2\right|\left|\overset{\to}{a}3\right|\right\}$

Hence, $\left(B\right)$ is also true.

& W_C=5 \mathrm{eV}\end{aligned}$
Since, $W_A \lt W$ and $W_B \lt W$, hence, $A and B$ will emit photoelectrons.

46586.text: The radius of gyration of a body about an axis at a distance 6 cm from its centre of mass is 10 cm . Then, its radius of gyration about a parallel axis through its centre of mass will be
46586.sol:
From the theorem of parallel axis, the moment of inertia $I$ is equal to
$I=I_{\mathrm{CM}}+M a^2$
where $I_{\mathrm{CM}}$ is moment of inertia about centre of mass and $a$ the distance of axis from centre.
$\therefore \quad I=M K^2+M \times(6)^2$
$M K_1^2=M K^2+36 M$
$\Rightarrow \quad K_1^2=K^2+36$
$\Rightarrow \quad(10)^2=K^2+36$
$\Rightarrow \quad K^2=100-36=64$
$\Rightarrow \quad K=8 \mathrm{~cm}$

46882.subject: Zoology
46882.text: Bile helps in the digestion of fat through
46882.sol: Bile contains no digestive enzymes, yet it plays an important role in fat digestion. It intensifies the 'mixing contractions' of intestinal wall. The organic salts by bile reduce the surface tension of fats globules and suspend them in water of digestive juice. It is emulsification of fats. It facilitates easy action of pancreatic juice on fats. They also help in formation of micelles which help to transport of all and products of fat digestion from intestinal lumen to absorptive cells. The inorganic bile salts import alkalinity to chyme and inactivate gastric pepsin.

Cleistogamous flowers are flowers that do not open at all. In such flowers, the anthers and stigma lie close to each other, and they are not exposed. Thus, statement (a) is incorrect.

Since these flowers never open, they are invariably autogamous (strictly self-pollinating) and there is no chance of cross-pollen landing on the stigma. Therefore, they do not require pollinators. Thus, statement (c) is incorrect.

Because of strict autogamy, they produce an assured seed set even in the absence of pollinators. Thus, statement (b) is correct.

As they undergo only self-pollination, there is no mixing of genetic material from different individuals, which means variations in traits are generally not seen in the next generation. Thus, statement (d) is correct.

Therefore, statements (b) and (d) are correct.

Answer: Statements (b) and (d) are correct

50881.text: $\mathrm{y}=3 \sin \pi \left(\frac{\mathrm{t}}{2}-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{4}\right) represents an equation of a progressive wave, where $ t$ is in second and $x$ is in metre. The distance travelled by the wave in 5 \mathrm{ s}$ is
50881.sol:
The given equation of a progressive wave is $y=3 \sin \pi\left(\frac{t}{2}-\frac{x}{4}\right)=3 \sin 2 \pi\left(\frac{t}{4}-\frac{x}{8}\right)$
The standard equation of a progressive wave is
$$
\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{y}_{0} \sin 2 \pi\left(\frac{\mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{T}}-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\lambda}\right)
$$
Comparing these two equations, we get
$$
\mathrm{T}=4 \mathrm{~s}, \lambda=8 \mathrm{~m}
$$
$\therefore$ Velocity of wave,
$$
\mathrm{v}=\frac{\lambda}{\mathrm{T}}=\frac{8}{4}=2 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}
$$
Distance travelled by wave in time $t$ is
$$
\mathrm{s}=\mathrm{vt}
$$
or
$$
\mathrm{s}=2 \times 5=10 \mathrm{~m}
$$

58236.subject: Chemistry
58236.text: Which of the following is an acidic oxide?
58236.sol:
Oxide classification depends on the element's position in the periodic table and its oxidation state. Non-metal oxides are typically acidic while metal oxides are basic, though exceptions exist such as neutral oxides.

Carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$), nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$), and nitrous oxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}$) are all neutral oxides that do not react with acids or bases.

Dinitrogen pentoxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$) is acidic, reacting with water to form nitric acid: $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{HNO}_3$. It also forms salts with bases.

Thus, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is the acidic oxide among the options.

60226.subject: Mathematics
60226.text: If the function $f(x) = ax^3 + bx^2 + 11x - 6$, defined on $[1,3]$, satisfies all the conditions of Rolle's theorem for $c = 2 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$, then
60226.sol:
Since $f(x)$ satisfies Rolle's theorem on $[1, 3]$, we must have $f(1) = f(3)$.

$f(1) = a(1)^3 + b(1)^2 + 11(1) - 6 = a + b + 5$

$f(3) = a(3)^3 + b(3)^2 + 11(3) - 6 = 27a + 9b + 27$

Equating $f(1)$ and $f(3)$:

$a + b + 5 = 27a + 9b + 27$

$26a + 8b + 22 = 0 \Rightarrow 13a + 4b + 11 = 0$

By Rolle's theorem, $f'(c) = 0$ for $c = 2 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

$f'(x) = 3ax^2 + 2bx + 11$

$f'\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = 3a\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2 + 2b\left(2 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + 11 = 0$

$3a\left(4 + \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + 4b + \dfrac{2b}{\sqrt{3}} + 11 = 0$

$13a + 4\sqrt{3}a + 4b + \dfrac{2b}{\sqrt{3}} + 11 = 0$

$(13a + 4b + 11) + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(12a + 2b) = 0$

Substituting $13a + 4b + 11 = 0$ into the above equation:

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(12a + 2b) = 0 \Rightarrow 12a + 2b = 0 \Rightarrow b = -6a$

Substituting $b = -6a$ into $13a + 4b + 11 = 0$:

$13a + 4(-6a) + 11 = 0$

$-11a + 11 = 0 \Rightarrow a = 1$

$b = -6(1) = -6$

Answer: $a = 1, b = -6$

60726.text: The angle between the tangents drawn from the origin to the circle $(x-7)^2+(y+1)^2=25$ is
60726.sol: Equation of the circle: $(x-7)^2+(y+1)^2=25$ Center is at $(7,-1)$ with radius $r=5$. The tangents originate from the point $P=(0,0)$. Distance from $P$ to center is $d=\sqrt{(7-0)^2+(-1-0)^2}=\sqrt{49+1}=\sqrt{50}$. The tangent at any point is perpendicular to the radius at that point, forming a right triangle with sides $r=5$, $d=\sqrt{50}$, and tangent length. Let $\theta$ be the angle between the two tangents. Then $\sin(\theta/2)=r/d$. $\theta/2=\arcsin(5/\sqrt{50})=\arcsin(1/\sqrt{2})=\pi/4\theta=2(\pi/4)=\pi/2$ radians Converting to decimal: $\pi/2\approx1.5708$ radians.

62013.subject: Mathematics
62013.sol:
To determine the parity of $f(x)=\sec\left[\log\left(x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right)\right]$, we evaluate $f(-x)$:

$f(-x) = \sec\left[\log\left(-x+\sqrt{1+(-x)^{2}}\right)\right] = \sec\left[\log\left(-x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right)\right]$

Observe that the product $\left(x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right)\left(-x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right) = (1+x^{2}) - x^{2} = 1$, which implies:

$-x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}} = \frac{1}{x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}$

Substituting back:

$f(-x) = \sec\left[\log\left(\frac{1}{x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}\right)\right]$

Applying the logarithmic identity $\log(1/A) = -\log A$:

$f(-x) = \sec\left[-\log\left(x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right)\right]$

Since secant is an even function $(\sec(-\theta) = \sec\theta)$, we obtain:

$f(-x) = \sec\left[\log\left(x+\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\right)\right] = f(x)$

This equality $f(-x) = f(x)$ confirms that the function is even.

$\boxed{A}$

62128.subject: Mathematics
62128.text: If the line $4x + 3y = 7$ touches the hyperbola $x^2 - y^2 = 7$, then the sum of the co-ordinates of the point of contact is...
62128.sol:
The equation of the given hyperbola is $x^2 - y^2 = 7$.

Let the point of contact be $(x_1, y_1)$. The equation of the tangent to the hyperbola at this point is given by $x x_1 - y y_1 = 7$.

The given equation of the line is $4x + 3y = 7$.

Since both equations represent the same tangent line, we can compare their corresponding coefficients:

$x_1 = 4$

$-y_1 = 3 \Rightarrow y_1 = -3$

The point of contact is $(4,-3)$.

The sum of the coordinates of the point of contact is $4 + (-3) = 1$.

Answer: $1$

62519.subject: Mathematics
62519.text: If $3\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 + x^2}\right) - 4\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 + x^2}\right) + 2\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 - x^2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ then $x = ?$
62519.sol:
Assuming $0 < x < 1$, the standard inverse trigonometric identities are:

$\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 + x^2}\right) = 2\tan^{-1}x$

$\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 + x^2}\right) = 2\tan^{-1}x$

$\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1 - x^2}\right) = 2\tan^{-1}x$

Substituting these into the given equation yields:

$3(2\tan^{-1}x) - 4(2\tan^{-1}x) + 2(2\tan^{-1}x) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$6\tan^{-1}x - 8\tan^{-1}x + 4\tan^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$2\tan^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\tan^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$x = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Since $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ satisfies the condition $0 < x < 1$, it is the valid solution.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

62817.subject: Mathematics
62817.text: The region satisfying the inequalities $y - x \geq 2,\ x + y \leq 5,\ x \geq 0$ and $y \geq 0$ is
62817.sol:
The given inequalities are:
$y - x \geq 2$
$x + y \leq 5$
$x \geq 0$
$y \geq 0$

Let us plot the corresponding lines to find the bounded region:
1. The line $y - x = 2$ intersects the y-axis at $(0, 2)$ and the x-axis at $(-2, 0)$. The inequality $y - x \geq 2$ (or $y \geq x + 2$) represents the region above this line.
2. The line $x + y = 5$ intersects the y-axis at $(0, 5)$ and the x-axis at $(5, 0)$. The inequality $x + y \leq 5$ (or $y \leq -x + 5$) represents the region below this line.
3. $x \geq 0$ represents the region to the right of the y-axis.
4. $y \geq 0$ represents the region above the x-axis.

Finding the point of intersection of the two lines:
$y - x = 2$
$y + x = 5$
Adding the two equations, we get $2y = 7 \Rightarrow y = 3.5$.
Substituting $y$ in the second equation, $x = 1.5$.
The lines intersect at $(1.5, 3.5)$.

This forms a triangular region with vertices at $(0, 2)$, $(0, 5)$, and $(1.5, 3.5)$.

62842.text: The feasible region represented by the given constraints $2 x+3 \mathrm{y} \geqslant 12,-x+\mathrm{y} \leqslant 3, x \leqslant 4, \mathrm{y} \geqslant 3$ is denoted by
62842.sol:
To determine the feasible region satisfying all inequalities, analyze the constraints using boundary lines and the origin as a test point.

The inequality $2x + 3y \ge 12$ defines the region above the line $2x + 3y = 12$, as the origin $(0,0)$ yields $0 \not\ge 12$.
The constraint $-x + y \le 3$ corresponds to the region below $-x + y = 3$, since $(0,0)$ gives $0 \le 3$.
$x \le 4$ is satisfied to the left of $x = 4$, as $0 \le 4$ at the origin.
$y \ge 3$ requires the region above $y = 3$, with $(0,0)$ not satisfying $0 \ge 3$.

Combining these: $y \ge 3$ eliminates regions $S_2$ and $S_3$, leaving $S_1$ and $S_4$. Both satisfy $x \le 4$.
$-x + y \le 3$ excludes $S_1$ (above the line) and retains $S_4$ (below it).
$2x + 3y \ge 12$ holds for $S_4$, verified by point $(2,4)$ yielding $16 \ge 12$, and the intersection of $2x + 3y = 12$ with $y = 3$ at $x = 1.5$ confirms $S_4$ is entirely above this line.

The feasible region is $\boxed{\text{S}_4}$.

63332.text: If the distance between the lines represented by $(x - 2y)^2 + k(x - 2y) = 0$ is $3$ units and $k > 0$ then the equations of the lines are
63332.sol:
The given equation is $(x - 2y)^2 + k(x - 2y) = 0$.

Factoring the equation, we get:

$(x - 2y)(x - 2y + k) = 0$

This represents two parallel lines:

$x - 2y = 0$

$x - 2y + k = 0$

The distance between two parallel lines $ax + by + c_1 = 0$ and $ax + by + c_2 = 0$ is given by $\dfrac{|c_1 - c_2|}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$.

Applying this formula, the distance between the lines is:

$d = \dfrac{|k - 0|}{\sqrt{1^2 + (-2)^2}} = \dfrac{|k|}{\sqrt{5}}$

Given that the distance is $3$ units:

$\dfrac{|k|}{\sqrt{5}} = 3 \Rightarrow |k| = 3\sqrt{5}$

Since $k > 0$, we have $k = 3\sqrt{5}$.

Substituting the value of $k$, the equations of the lines are $x - 2y = 0$ and $x - 2y + 3\sqrt{5} = 0$.

Answer: $x - 2y = 0$ and $x - 2y + 3\sqrt{5} = 0$.

63554.text: In a certain city, the ratio of men to women is $5:4$. It is found that $80\%$ of men and $90\%$ of women are literate. If a person selected at random is found to be illiterate, then the probability that the person is a man is....
63554.sol:
Let $M$ and $W$ be the events that the selected person is a man and a woman respectively.

$P(M) = \dfrac{5}{9}$ and $P(W) = \dfrac{4}{9}$

Let $I$ be the event that the selected person is illiterate.

Given that $80\%$ of men and $90\%$ of women are literate, the probabilities of them being illiterate are:

$P(I|M) = 1 - 0.8 = 0.2 = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$P(I|W) = 1 - 0.9 = 0.1 = \dfrac{1}{10}$

By Bayes' theorem, the probability that the person is a man given that they are illiterate is:

$P(M|I) = \dfrac{P(M)P(I|M)}{P(M)P(I|M) + P(W)P(I|W)}$

$P(M|I) = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{9} \times \dfrac{1}{5}}{\dfrac{5}{9} \times \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{4}{9} \times \dfrac{1}{10}}$

$P(M|I) = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{9}}{\dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{2}{45}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{45}}{\dfrac{7}{45}} = \dfrac{5}{7}$

63626.text:
If a random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution of $X
X= x01234567
P(X= x)0 k2 k2 k3 k k^22 k^27 k^2+k
\) Then \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X} \geqslant 6)=$
63626.sol:
The sum of probabilities in the distribution must be 1: $P(X=0) + P(X=1) + P(X=2) + P(X=3) + P(X=4) + P(X=5) + P(X=6) + P(X=7) = 1$.

Substituting the given expressions: $0 + k + 2k + 2k + 3k + k^2 + 2k^2 + (7k^2 + k) = 1$.

Combining like terms yields $10k^2 + 9k = 1$, which rearranges to the quadratic equation $10k^2 + 9k - 1 = 0$.

Factoring gives $(10k - 1)(k + 1) = 0$, with solutions $k = \frac{1}{10}$ or $k = -1$. Since probability must be non-negative, $k = \frac{1}{10}$.

To find $P(X \geq 6)$, sum $P(X=6) + P(X=7)$:

$P(X=6) = 2k^2 = 2(\frac{1}{10})^2 = \frac{2}{100}$

$P(X=7) = 7k^2 + k = 7(\frac{1}{10})^2 + \frac{1}{10} = \frac{17}{100}$

$P(X \geq 6) = \frac{2}{100} + \frac{17}{100} = \frac{19}{100}$

This matches option A.

$\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=x)=\mathrm{k}(x+1)\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^x$, where k is a constant. Then $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{X}=0)$ is
63652.sol:
To determine $P(X=0)$, the normalizing constant $k$ must first be found using the probability distribution constraint. The sum over all $x$ gives $\sum_{x=0}^{\infty} k(x+1)\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^x = 1$.

The series $\sum_{x=0}^{\infty} (x+1)r^x$ converges to $\frac{1}{(1-r)^2}$ for $|r| < 1$. With $r = \frac{1}{5}$, this yields $\frac{1}{(1 - \frac{1}{5})^2} = \frac{1}{(\frac{4}{5})^2} = \frac{25}{16}$.

This gives $k \cdot \frac{25}{16} = 1$, so $k = \frac{16}{25}$.

Then $P(X=0) = k(0+1)\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^0 = k \cdot 1 \cdot 1 = \frac{16}{25}$.

The value matches option A.

63983.subject: Mathematics
63983.text: In a triangle $A B C$, with usual notations, if $a=5, b=4, \cos (A-B)=\frac{31}{32}$, then $c=$
63983.sol:
Given: In a triangle, sides $a = 5$, $b = 4$, and $\cos(A - B) = \frac{31}{32}$. Find side $c$.

Using the identity $\cos(A - B) = \cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B$, express the trigonometric functions in terms of the sides via the cosine rule:

$\cos A = \frac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc} = \frac{16 + c^2 - 25}{8c} = \frac{c^2 - 9}{8c}$

$\cos B = \frac{a^2 + c^2 - b^2}{2ac} = \frac{25 + c^2 - 16}{10c} = \frac{c^2 + 9}{10c}$

Using the sine rule, $\sin A = \frac{a \sin C}{c} = \frac{5 \sin C}{c}$ and $\sin B = \frac{b \sin C}{c} = \frac{4 \sin C}{c}$.

Substitute into the identity:

$\frac{31}{32} = \left(\frac{c^2 - 9}{8c}\right)\left(\frac{c^2 + 9}{10c}\right) + \left(\frac{5 \sin C}{c}\right)\left(\frac{4 \sin C}{c}\right) = \frac{c^4 - 81}{80c^2} + \frac{20 \sin^2 C}{c^2}$

Now express $\sin^2 C$ in terms of $c$ using $\cos C = \frac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} = \frac{41 - c^2}{40}$:

$\sin^2 C = 1 - \left(\frac{41 - c^2}{40}\right)^2 = \frac{1600 - (41 - c^2)^2}{1600}$

Substitute back:

$\frac{31}{32} = \frac{c^4 - 81}{80c^2} + \frac{1}{c^2} \cdot \frac{20[1600 - (41 - c^2)^2]}{1600} = \frac{c^4 - 81}{80c^2} + \frac{1600 - (41 - c^2)^2}{80c^2}$

Combine terms:

$\frac{31}{32} = \frac{c^4 - 81 + 1600 - (1681 - 82c^2 + c^4)}{80c^2} = \frac{82c^2 - 162}{80c^2} = \frac{41c^2 - 81}{40c^2}$

Cross-multiply:

$31 \cdot 40c^2 = 32(41c^2 - 81)$
$1240c^2 = 1312c^2 - 2592$
$72c^2 = 2592$
$c^2 = 36$

Thus, $c = 6$.

Solution: $\boxed{6}$

64196.text: The family of straight lines $4ax + 3by + c = 0$ such that $a + b + c = 0$ (where a, b, c are real constants) are concurrent at the point...
64196.sol:
Given the family of straight lines $4ax + 3by + c = 0$ and the condition $a + b + c = 0$.

Substituting $c = -(a + b)$ into the equation of the line:

$4ax + 3by - (a + b) = 0$

$a(4x - 1) + b(3y - 1) = 0$

For the lines to be concurrent for all values of $a and b$, the coefficients of $a and b$ must be zero.

$4x - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$3y - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{1}{3}$

The point of concurrency is $\left(\dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

64368.text: The angle between the line $x - 1 = 2 - y = \dfrac{2z - 6}{4}$ and the plane $\vec{r} \cdot (2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 10$ is
64368.sol:
The equation of the line can be rewritten in standard form as:

$\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y - 2}{-1} = \dfrac{z - 3}{2}$

The direction vector of the line is $\vec{b} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$.

The equation of the plane is $\vec{r} \cdot (2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 10$.

The normal vector to the plane is $\vec{n} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

The angle $\theta$ between the line and the plane is given by:

$\sin \theta = \dfrac{|\vec{b} \cdot \vec{n}|}{|\vec{b}| |\vec{n}|}$

$\sin \theta = \dfrac{|(1)(2) + (-1)(1) + (2)(1)|}{\sqrt{1^2 + (-1)^2 + 2^2} \sqrt{2^2 + 1^2 + 1^2}}$

$\sin \theta = \dfrac{|2 - 1 + 2|}{\sqrt{6} \sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

68603.text: The ratio of the density of oxygen nucleus $({}^{16}_{8}\text{O})$ and helium nucleus $({}^{4}_{2}\text{He})$ is
68603.sol:
The radius of a nucleus with mass number $A$ is given by $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$.

The volume of the nucleus is $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A$.

The mass of the nucleus is $M \approx A m$, where $m$ is the average mass of a nucleon.

The density of the nucleus is $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{A m}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A} = \dfrac{m}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3}$.

Since the density is independent of the mass number $A$, it is constant for all nuclei.

Therefore, the ratio of the density of the oxygen nucleus to the helium nucleus is $1 : 1$.

Answer: $1 : 1$

From the given logic circuit, the gates can be identified as follows:
1. A NOT gate with input $A$, giving output $\bar{A}$.
2. An AND gate with inputs $B$ and $C$, giving output $B \cdot C$.
3. An OR gate taking the outputs of the NOT and AND gates as inputs.

The Boolean expression for the final output $Y$ is:
$Y = \bar{A} + B \cdot C$

For the output to be $Y = 1$, either $\bar{A} = 1$ (which means $A = 0$) or $B \cdot C = 1$ (which means $B = 1$ and $C = 1$).

Since all given options have $A = 1$, we have $\bar{A} = 0$.
Thus, for $Y = 1$, the condition $B \cdot C = 1$ must be satisfied, which requires $B = 1$ and $C = 1$.

Therefore, the correct input combination is $A = 1$, $B = 1$, $C = 1$.

Answer: $A = 1$ , $B = 1$ , $C = 1$

In a Young's double slit experiment, the intensities at two points, for the path difference $\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$ and $\dfrac{\lambda}{3}$ ($\lambda$ being the wavelength of light used) are $I_1 and I_2$ respectively. 70166.sol:
The phase difference $\phi$ is related to the path difference $\Delta x$ by the formula $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$.

The resultant intensity in a Young's double slit experiment when both slits have intensity $I_0$ is given by:
$I = 4I_0 \cos^2 \left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)

For a path difference of \Delta$x_1 = $\dfrac{\lambda}{4}:
$\phi_1 = $\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \dfrac{\lambda}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}
\dfrac{\phi_1}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{4} =45^{}^{\circ}$
$I_1 = 4I_0 \cos^2(45^{}^{\circ}) = 4I_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 = 4I_0 \times \dfrac{1}{2} =2I_0$

For a path difference of \Delta$ x_2 = \dfrac{\lambda}{3}:
$\phi_2 = $\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \dfrac{\lambda}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}
\dfrac{\phi_2}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} =60^{}^{\circ}$
$I_2 = 4I_0 \cos^2(60^{}^{\circ}) = 4I_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 4I_0 \times \dfrac{1}{4} =$ I_0$

Adding the two intensities:
$I_1 + I_2 = 2I_0 + I_0 = 3I_0$

Therefore, the required ratio is:
\dfrac{I_1 + I_2}{I_0} = \dfrac{3I_0}{I_0} =3$

70457.subject: Physics
70457.text: The equation of a progressive wave is $Y = 3 \sin \left[\pi  \left(\dfrac{t}{3} - \dfrac{x}{5}\right) + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]where X and Y are in metre and time in second. Which of the following is correct?$
70457.sol:
The given equation of the progressive wave is $Y = 3 \sin \left[\pi \left(\dfrac{t}{3} - \dfrac{x}{5}\right) + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]

Rewriting$ the equation, we getY = 3 \sin$\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{3} - \dfrac{\pi x}{5} + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

Comparing this with the standard equation of a progressive wave $Y = A \sin(\omegat - kx + \phi)$, we get:

Amplitude $A = 3$ m $= 300$ cm

Angular frequency $\omega = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$rad/s

Wave number $k = \dfrac{\pi}{5}$rad/m

Wavelength $\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi}{k} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\pi/5} =10$ m

Wave velocity $v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \dfrac{\pi/3}{\pi/5} = \dfrac{5}{3} \approx1.67$ m/s

Frequency $f = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi} = \dfrac{\pi/3}{2\pi} = \dfrac{1}{6} \approx0.167$ Hz

Thus, the only correct statement is that the wavelength is $10$ m.

Answer: Wavelength = $10$ m

72108.subject: Physics
72108.text: In hydrogen spectrum the ratio of wavelengths of the last line of Lyman series and the last line of Balmer series is
72108.sol:
The wavelength of a spectral line in the hydrogen spectrum is given by Rydberg's formula:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right)

For$ the last line of the Lyman series, the transition is from n_2 = $\infty$ to n_1 = 1$.

\dfrac{1}{\lambda_L} =$ R $\left( \dfrac{1}{1^2} - \dfrac{1}{\infty^2} \right) =$ R$

$\lambda_L = $\dfrac{1}{R}

For$ the last line of the Balmer series, the transition is from n_2 = $\infty$ to n_1 = 2$.

\dfrac{1}{\lambda_B} =$ R $\left( \dfrac{1}{2^2} - \dfrac{1}{\infty^2} \right) = \dfrac{R}{4}

$\lambda_B = $\dfrac{4}{R}

The ratio$ of $the wavelengths is:

\dfrac{\lambda_L}{\lambda_B} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{R}}{\dfrac{4}{R}} = \dfrac{1}{4} =0.25$

Answer: $0.25$

72169.subject: Physics
72169.text: Two identical inductors are connected in parallel. If the parallel combination stores $40\ \text{J}$ of magnetic field energy when a total current of $2\ \text{A}$ is passed through it, the value of the self-inductance of each coil is
72169.sol:
Let the self-inductance of each coil be $L$.

Since the two identical inductors are connected in parallel, their equivalent inductance $L_{eq}$ is given by:

$L_{eq} = \dfrac{L}{2}$

The magnetic potential energy stored in the equivalent inductor is:

$U = \dfrac{1}{2} L_{eq} I^2$

Given $U = 40\ \text{J}$ and total current $I = 2\ \text{A}$, substituting these values:

$40 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right) (2)^2$

$40 = \dfrac{L}{4} \times 4$

$L = 40\ \text{H}$

Answer: $40\ \text{H}$

79429.text:
A group of researchers procured some fish-like animals and upon investigation the following characters were observed :

B. Ectoparasitic, as they were found attached on fish skin with their circular sucking mouth.

79429.sol:
The given characteristics belong to the class Cyclostomata.

Members of this class are ectoparasites on some fishes. They have an elongated body bearing $6-15$ pairs of gill slits for respiration.

Cyclostomes have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws.

Their body is devoid of scales and paired fins.

Cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous.

Petromyzon (Lamprey) and Myxine (Hagfish) are examples of class Cyclostomata.

Scoliodon belongs to class Chondrichthyes.

Exocoetus belongs to class Osteichthyes.

Branchiostoma belongs to subphylum Cephalochordata.

Thus, Petromyzon sp. fits best with the given characters.

Answer: Petromyzon sp.

80449.subject: Botany
80449.text: During which stage in the complete oxidation of glucose arc the greatest number of ATP molecules formed from ADP?
options: conversion of pyruvic acid to acetyl CoA
80449.sol:
The electron transport chain is primarily used to send protons across the membrane into the intermembrane space. This create a proton-motive force, which will drive ATP synthase in the final step of cellular respiration to create ATP from ADP and a phosphate group.
Related Theory
In chemiosmosis, the free energy from the series of redox reactions just described is used to pump hydrogen ions across the membrane. The uneven distribution of $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ions across the membrane establishes both concentration and electrical gradients, owing to the hydrogen ions' positive charge and their aggregation on one side of the membrane. If the membrane were open to diffusion by the hydrogen ions, the ions would tend to diffuse back across into the matrix, driven by their electrochemical gradient. Similarly, hydrogen ions in the matrix space can only pass through the inner mitochondrial membrane through an integral membrane protein called ATP synthase. This complex protein acts as a tiny generator, turned by the force of the hydrogen ions diffusing through it, down their electrochemical gradient. The turning of parts of this molecular machine facilitates the addition of a phosphate to ADP, forming ATP, using the potential energy of the hydrogen ion gradient.

81013.subject: Chemistry
81013.text: For a certain reaction $R \rightarrow$ Product, the plot of concentration $[R]$ vs time has a negative slope as shown. The order of reaction is :
81013.sol:
From the given graph, the plot of concentration $[R]$ versus time $t$ is a straight line with a negative slope.

The equation for this straight line can be written as:
$y = mx + c$
$[R] = (\text{slope}) \times t + \text{intercept}$

Given that the intercept is $[R_0]$ and the slope is $-k$, the equation becomes:
$[R] = -kt + [R_0]$

This equation represents the integrated rate law for a zero-order reaction. For a zero-order reaction, the rate of reaction is independent of the concentration of the reactant:
$\text{Rate} = -\dfrac{d[R]}{dt} = k[R]^0 = k$

Integrating both sides:
$\int_{[R_0]}^{[R]} d[R] = -k \int_0^t dt$
$[R] - [R_0] = -kt$
$[R] = -kt + [R_0]$

Since the graph matches this equation, the order of the reaction is $0$.

Answer: $0$

82193.text:
In the first excited state of hydrogen atom, the energy of its electron is $-3.4$ eV. The radial distance of the electron from the hydrogen nucleus in this case is approximately :
(Take $1$ eV $= 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ J, $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C and $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^{9}$ N m$^2$/C$^2$)
82193.sol:
The total energy of an electron in a hydrogen atom is given by $E = -\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{e^2}{2r}$

Substituting the given values:

$-3.4 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} = -\dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times (1.6 \times 10^{-19})^2}{2r}$

$r = \dfrac{9 \times 10^9 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{2 \times 3.4}$

$r = \dfrac{14.4 \times 10^{-10}}{6.8}$

$r \approx 2.117 \times 10^{-10}$ m

This is approximately $2.1 \times 10^{-10}$ m.

Answer: $2.1 \times 10^{-10}$ m

84575.subject: Zoology
84575.text:
Arrange the following cell layers/structures around the female gamete, from outer to inner side :
A. Zona pellucida
B. Perivitelline space
C. Corona radiata
D. Plasma membrane of ovum
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
84575.sol:
The mature female gamete (ovum) is surrounded by several layers. From the outermost to the innermost side, the arrangement is as follows:

Corona radiata: The outermost layer consisting of follicle cells.

Zona pellucida: A non-cellular glycoprotein layer situated just inside the corona radiata.

Perivitelline space: The narrow space between the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane of the ovum.

Plasma membrane of ovum (Oolemma): The innermost boundary enclosing the cytoplasm of the ovum.

Therefore, the correct sequence from outer to inner side is Corona radiata (C), Zona pellucida (A), Perivitelline space (B), and Plasma membrane of ovum (D).

Answer: C, A, B, D

86537.text:
A possible solution of the system of equations
$x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2 = 0$
$(\log_{10} x)^2 + 2(\log_{10} x)(\log_{10} y) + (\log_{10} y)^2 = 4$
is
86537.sol:
The first equation is $x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2 = 0$

$(x - 4y)^2 = 0$

$x = 4y$

The second equation is $(\log_{10} x)^2 + 2(\log_{10} x)(\log_{10} y) + (\log_{10} y)^2 = 4$

$(\log_{10} x + \log_{10} y)^2 = 4$

$\log_{10} (xy) = \pm 2$

$xy = 10^2 = 100$ or $xy = 10^{-2} = \dfrac{1}{100}$

Substituting $x = 4y$ into $xy = 100$ gives $4y^2 = 100 \Rightarrow y^2 = 25$. Since $y > 0$, $y = 5$ and $x = 20$.

Substituting $x = 4y$ into $xy = \dfrac{1}{100}$ gives $4y^2 = \dfrac{1}{100} \Rightarrow y^2 = \dfrac{1}{400}$. Since $y > 0$, $y = \dfrac{1}{20}$ and $x = \dfrac{1}{5}$.

Therefore, a possible solution is $x = \dfrac{1}{5}, y = \dfrac{1}{20}$.

Answer: $x = \dfrac{1}{5},\ y = \dfrac{1}{20}$

89211.sol:
Packing fraction in hcp $= \dfrac{6 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3}}{Volume}$

$= \dfrac{6 \times 4\pi{r}^{3}}{3 \times Area \times Height}$

Area (of base) of unit cell in hcp $= 6\sqrt{3}{r}^{2}$ (follow text)

height of unit cell in hcp $= 4r \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}$ (follow text)

So packing fraction $= \dfrac{6 \times 4\pi{r}^{3}}{3 \times 6\sqrt{3}{r}^{2} \times 4r \times \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}}$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{3\sqrt{2}} = 0.74$

or = 74%

Thus, empty space in hcp = 1 - 0.74 = 0.26

or = 26%.

91501.text: Number of words that can be formed with the letters of the word $ALGEBRA$ so that all the vowels are separated (or no two vowels come together) is
91501.sol:
Vowels are $A, E, A$
Consonants are $L, G, B, R$
$XLXGXBXRX$
Since there is no restriction on consonants, we must place them first and they can be arranged in $4 ! = 24$ days.
Now to arrange vowels so that no two of them are together we have $5$ places $\left(X\right) .$ Out of these $5$ places, $3$ can be selected in ${}^{5}{C}_{3}$ ways and then one arrangement can be made in $\dfrac{3 !}{2 !}$ ways.
Thus, required ways $= 4 ! \times {}^{5}{C}_{3} \times \dfrac{3 !}{2 !} = 720$

102662.subject: Physics
102662.text: A closed organ pipe is maintained at an absolute temperature $T_1$, and an open organ pipe of the exact same length is maintained at an absolute temperature $T_2$. Both pipes are filled with the same gas. If the fundamental frequencies of the two pipes are equal, what is the ratio of their absolute temperatures $T_1 : T_2$?
102662.sol:
The fundamental frequency of a closed organ pipe of length $L$ is given by $f_c = \dfrac{v_1}{4L}$.

The fundamental frequency of an open organ pipe of the same length $L$ is given by $f_o = \dfrac{v_2}{2L}$.

The speed of sound in a gas is $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma RT}{M}}$. Since the gas is the same, $v \propto \sqrt{T}$.

Given that the fundamental frequencies are equal, we have:
$\dfrac{v_1}{4L} = \dfrac{v_2}{2L}$

$\dfrac{v_1}{4} = \dfrac{v_2}{2}$

$\dfrac{v_1}{v_2} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2$

Substituting the proportionality of speed with temperature:
$\sqrt{\dfrac{T_1}{T_2}} = 2$

Squaring both sides yields:
$\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = 4$

Thus, the ratio $T_1 : T_2$ is $4:1$.

Answer: $4:1$

102870.subject: Physics
102870.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor.

Reason (R): In a static situation, the electric field inside the conductor is zero and has no tangential component on its surface.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
102870.sol:
In a static situation, the electric field inside a conductor is zero. Since $E = -\dfrac{dV}{dr}$, a zero electric field implies that the electrostatic potential $V$ is constant throughout the volume of the conductor, but it is not necessarily zero. It is equal to the potential on the surface. Thus, the Assertion is incorrect.

The Reason is correct because in electrostatics, free charges inside the conductor redistribute to make the internal electric field zero. Additionally, the electric field at the surface must be normal to the surface, meaning it has no tangential component; otherwise, surface charges would experience a force and move.

Answer: (A) is incorrect but (R) is correct

103010.text: A certain charge $Q$ is divided into two parts $q$ and $Q-q$. How the charge $Q$ and $q$ must be related so that when $q$ and $(Q-q)$ is placed at a certain distance apart experience maximum electrostatic repulsion?
103010.sol:
The electrostatic force of repulsion between the charge $q$ and $(Q-q)$ at separation $r$ is given by
$F=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q(Q-q)}{r^2}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q Q-q^2}{r^2}$
If $F$ is maximum, then $\partial F / \partial q=0$ i.e. $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{(Q-2 q)}{r^2}=0$
As $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 r^2}$ is constant, therefore
$Q-2 q=0$ or $Q=2 q$

103933.subject: Physics
103933.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the change in self-inductance of an ideal air-cored solenoid when its parameters are modified.

List-IList-II
(A) Doubling total turns and doubling length, keeping area constant(I) Inductance becomes $4$ times
(B) Doubling turns per unit length and doubling length, keeping area constant(II) Inductance becomes $2$ times
(C) Halving total turns, keeping length and area constant(III) Inductance becomes $\dfrac{1}{4}$ times
(D) Inserting a magnetic core of relative permeability $4$, keeping dimensions constant(IV) Inductance becomes $8$ times

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
103933.sol:
The self-inductance of a solenoid in terms of total turns $N$ is $L = \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l}$.
In terms of turns per unit length $n$ ($n = \dfrac{N}{l}$), it is $L = \mu_0 n^2 A l$.

(A) Doubling $N$ and doubling $l$: $L' = \dfrac{\mu_0 (2N)^2 A}{2l} = 2 \left( \dfrac{\mu_0 N^2 A}{l} \right) = 2L$. (Matches II)

(B) Doubling $n$ and doubling $l$: $L' = \mu_0 (2n)^2 A (2l) = 8 (\mu_0 n^2 A l) = 8L$. (Matches IV)

(C) Halving $N$ only: $L' = \dfrac{\mu_0 (N/2)^2 A}{l} = \dfrac{1}{4} L$. (Matches III)

(D) Inserting a core of $\mu_r = 4$: $L' = \mu_0 \mu_r n^2 A l = 4L$. (Matches I)

Therefore, the correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (III), (D) - (I).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (IV), (C) - (III), (D) - (I)

104884.subject: Physics
104884.text: A hypothetical hydrogen-like atom consists of a proton and a negatively charged unknown particle. The ground state energy of this atom is found to be $-2720 \text{ eV}$. Given that the first Bohr radius of a normal hydrogen atom is $0.53 \text{ \AA}$ and its ground state energy is $-13.6 \text{ eV}$, what is the radius of the second Bohr orbit of this hypothetical atom?
104884.sol:
The energy of an electron in a Bohr orbit is directly proportional to the mass of the orbiting particle: $E \propto m$.

Let the mass of the unknown particle be $m_x$. The ratio of its mass to the electron's mass is:
$\dfrac{m_x}{m_e} = \dfrac{E_x}{E_e} = \dfrac{-2720 \text{ eV}}{-13.6 \text{ eV}} = 200$

Thus, $m_x = 200 m_e$.

The radius of a Bohr orbit is given by $r_n \propto \dfrac{n^2}{m}$.

For the first orbit ($n=1$) of the normal hydrogen atom:
$r_1 = 0.53 \text{ \AA}$

For the second orbit ($n=2$) of the hypothetical atom, the radius is:
$r_2' = r_1 \times \left(\dfrac{n^2}{1^2}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{m_e}{m_x}\right)$

$r_2' = 0.53 \times 4 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{200}\right) \text{ \AA}$

$r_2' = \dfrac{2.12}{200} \text{ \AA} = 0.0106 \text{ \AA}$

Converting to meters ($1 \text{ \AA} = 10^{-10} \text{ m}$):
$r_2' = 0.0106 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m} = 1.06 \times 10^{-12} \text{ m}$.

Answer: $1.06 \times 10^{-12} \text{ m}$

104999.subject: Physics
104999.text: A graph is plotted between the natural logarithm of the nuclear radius ($\ln R$) on the y-axis and the natural logarithm of the mass number ($\ln A$) on the x-axis for various nuclei. The resulting graph is a straight line. The slope of this straight line is:
104999.sol:
The relation between the nuclear radius $R$ and the mass number $A$ is given by:
$R = R_0 A^{1/3}$

Taking the natural logarithm on both sides, we get:
$\ln R = \ln R_0 + \dfrac{1}{3} \ln A$

Comparing this equation with the standard equation of a straight line, $y = mx + c$, where $y = \ln R$ and $x = \ln A$, we find:
Slope ($m$) = $\dfrac{1}{3}$
y-intercept ($c$) = $\ln R_0$

Therefore, the slope of the graph is $\dfrac{1}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{3}$

105276.subject: Physics
105276.text: A center-tap full-wave rectifier circuit uses two diodes $D_1$ and $D_2$ connected to the upper and lower ends of the secondary coil, respectively. The input AC voltage applied to the primary coil varies sinusoidally with time $t$, completing one full cycle in $40 \text{ ms}$, starting from zero with a positive slope at $t=0$. Consider four specific instants of time: $t=10 \text{ ms}$ (Point A), $t=20 \text{ ms}$ (Point B), $t=30 \text{ ms}$ (Point C), and $t=40 \text{ ms}$ (Point D). At which of these instants is diode $D_1$ reverse biased and diode $D_2$ forward biased?
105276.sol:
The input voltage has a time period $T = 40 \text{ ms}$.

During the first half-cycle ($0 < t < 20 \text{ ms}$), the input voltage is positive. This makes the upper end of the secondary coil positive with respect to the center tap, forward biasing diode $D_1$ and reverse biasing diode $D_2$. Point A ($t = 10 \text{ ms}$) falls in this interval.

During the second half-cycle ($20 \text{ ms} < t < 40 \text{ ms}$), the input voltage is negative. The upper end of the secondary coil becomes negative and the lower end becomes positive with respect to the center tap. This reverse biases diode $D_1$ and forward biases diode $D_2$. Point C ($t = 30 \text{ ms}$) falls in this interval.

At points B ($t = 20 \text{ ms}$) and D ($t = 40 \text{ ms}$), the input voltage is zero, so neither diode is forward biased.

Therefore, $D_1$ is reverse biased and $D_2$ is forward biased at Point C.

Answer: Point C

108628.subject: Chemistry
108628.text:
Consider the thermal decomposition of limestone:
$\text{CaCO}_{3}(\text{s}) \rightarrow \text{CaO}(\text{s}) + \text{CO}_{2}(\text{g})$

Under which of the following temperature conditions does this reaction become spontaneous?
108628.sol:
The thermal decomposition of limestone requires continuous heat input to break the bonds in $\text{CaCO}_{3}$, making it an endothermic process ($\Delta\text{H} > 0$).

The reaction produces a gaseous product ($\text{CO}_{2}$) from a solid reactant, which increases the randomness of the system. Therefore, the entropy change is positive ($\Delta\text{S} > 0$).

According to the Gibbs free energy equation, $\Delta\text{G} = \Delta\text{H} - \text{T}\Delta\text{S}$. For a process to be spontaneous, $\Delta\text{G}$ must be negative.

Since both $\Delta\text{H}$ and $\Delta\text{S}$ are positive, the term $\text{T}\Delta\text{S}$ must be greater than $\Delta\text{H}$ to make $\Delta\text{G} < 0$. This condition is satisfied only when the temperature is sufficiently high ($\text{T} > \dfrac{\Delta\text{H}}{\Delta\text{S}}$).

Answer: Spontaneous only at high temperatures

111883.subject: Chemistry
111883.text: When optically active (S)-2-bromooctane is treated with aqueous NaOH, the reaction proceeds exclusively via an $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ mechanism. What will be the stereochemical nature of the major product formed and the optical activity of the resulting reaction mixture?
options: Racemic mixture of octan-2-ol, optically inactive
111883.sol:
The $\text{S}_{\text{N}}2$ reaction involves the attack of the incoming nucleophile ($\text{OH}^{-}$) from the side opposite to the leaving group ($\text{Br}^{-}$).

This back-side attack leads to a complete inversion of configuration at the chiral center. Therefore, the reactant (S)-2-bromooctane will be converted entirely into (R)-octan-2-ol.

Because only a single enantiomer is formed as the product, the resulting reaction mixture will be optically active.

A racemic mixture would only form if the reaction proceeded via an $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ mechanism. A meso compound is impossible here because octan-2-ol has only one chiral center.

Answer: (R)-octan-2-ol, optically active

113518.subject: Chemistry
113518.text: An element germanium crystallises in $b c c$ type crystal structure with edge of unit cell equal to $288 \mathrm{pm}$ and the density of the element equal to $7.2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}$. The number of atoms present in $52 \mathrm{~g}$ of the crystalline element and the atomic mass of the element are respectively
113518.sol:
$d=7.2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}, a=288 \mathrm{pm}$ and mass of element $=52 \mathrm{~g}$
Hence, $d=\frac{\text{ Mass }}{\text{ Volume }} \Rightarrow 7.2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}=\frac{52 \mathrm{~g}}{V} V=\frac{52 \mathrm{~g}}{7.2 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~cm}^{-3}}=7.222 \mathrm{~cm}^3$
Edge of unit cell, $a=288 \mathrm{pm}=288 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~m}=288 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{~cm}=2.88 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~cm}$
Volume of unit cell, $a^3=\left(2.88 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{~cm}\right)^3=23.888 \times 10^{-24} \mathrm{~cm}^3$
The number of unit cells in $52 \mathrm{~g}$ of metal
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\text{ Total volume }}{\text{ Volume of one unit cell }} \\ & =\frac{7.222 \mathrm{~cm}^3}{23.888 \times 10^{-24} \mathrm{~cm}^3}=0.3023 \times 10^{24}\end{aligned}$
Germanium has body centred cubic structure. Hence, its unit cell contains 2 atoms.
$\therefore$ Total atoms in $3.023 \times 10^{23}$ unit cells are $2 \times 3.023 \times 10^{23}=6.046 \times 10^{23}$ atoms
Molar mass $=\frac{52 \mathrm{~g} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \text{ atom } \mathrm{mol}^{-1}}{6.046 \times 10^{23} \text{ atom }}$
Hence, atomic mass $=51.8$

121815.subject: Botany
121815.text: Where are sporangia located in Pteridophytes?
121815.sol: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves (Figure 3.3). These organs possess well-differentiated vascular tissues. The leaves in pteridophytes are small (microphylls) as in Selaginella or large (macrophylls) as in ferns. <mark>The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls</mark>. In some cases sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones (Selaginella, Equisetum). The sporangia produce spores by meiosis in spore mother cells.

Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size as in Chlamydomonas or non-flagellated and non-motile but similar in size as in Spirogyra. Fusion between one large, nonmotile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.

123480.subject: Botany
123480.text:
Assertion : In woody stems, the amount of heart wood continues to increase year after year.
Reason : The cambial activity continues uninterrupted.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
123480.sol: Heartwood formation occurs spontaneously because it is a genetically programmed process. As a result of continued secondary growth for several years, the older parts of the stem and its old branches have a part of its secondary xylem rendered non - functional. Such a modified and non - functional secondary xylem is called the heart wood or duramen, the functional outer younger rings of secondary xylem constitute the sap wood or alburnum. With the passage of time and addition of new outer rings of secondary xylem due to cambial activity more rings of the sap wood are changed into heart wood. This leads to the increase in the thickness of heart wood, whereas the sap wood remains of about the same thickness.

They are also involved in various growth inhibiting activities such as dormancy and abscission.

125456.subject: Botany
125456.text: What are bundle sheath cells in C4 plants rich in?
125456.sol: The primary CO2 acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) and is present in the mesophyll cells. The enzyme responsible for this fixation is PEP carboxylase or PEPcase. It is important to register that the mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO enzyme. The C4 acid OAA is formed in the mesophyll cells. It then forms other 4-carbon compounds like malic acid or aspartic acid in the mesophyll cells itself, which are transported to the bundle sheath cells. In the bundle sheath cells these C4 acids are broken down to release CO2 and a 3-carbon molecule. The 3-carbon molecule is transported back to the mesophyll where it is converted to PEP again, thus, completing the cycle.The CO2 released in the bundle sheath cells enters the C3 or the Calvin pathway, a pathway common to all plants. The bundle sheath cells are rich in an enzyme Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase (RuBisCO), but lack PEPcase. Thus, the basic pathway that results in the formation of the sugars, the Calvin pathway, is common to the C3 and C4 plants.

125460.subject: Botany
125460.text: In C3 plants, what is formed when RuBP binds with O2 instead of CO2?
options: 1 molecule of PGA and 1 molecule of phosphoglycolate
1 molecule of CO2 and 1 molecule of O2
125460.sol: Let us try and understand one more process that creates an important difference between C3 and C4 plants – Photorespiration. To understand photorespiration we have to know a little bit more about the first step of the Calvin pathway – the first CO2 fixation step. This is the reaction where RuBP combines with CO2 to form 2 molecules of 3PGA, that is catalysed by RuBisCO. In C3 plants some O2 does bind to RuBisCO, and hence CO2 fixation is decreased. Here the RuBP instead of being converted to 2 molecules of PGA binds with O2 to form one molecule of phosphoglycerate and phosphoglycolate (2 Carbon) in a pathway called photorespiration. In the photorespiratory pathway, there is neither synthesis of sugars, nor of ATP. Rather it results in the release of CO2 with the utilisation of ATP. In the photorespiratory pathway there is no synthesis of ATP or NADPH. The biological function of photorespiration is not known yet.

125647.subject: Botany
125647.text: During the biosynthetic phase of photosynthesis in a typical $C_{3}$ plant, if exactly 72 molecules of ATP are consumed, how many molecules of glucose are synthesized and how many molecules of NADPH are oxidized simultaneously?
options: 4 molecules of glucose and 48 molecules of NADPH
4 molecules of glucose and 24 molecules of NADPH
2 molecules of glucose and 48 molecules of NADPH
6 molecules of glucose and 72 molecules of NADPH
125647.sol:
In the biosynthetic phase of a $C_{3}$ plant, the synthesis of one molecule of glucose requires the fixation of 6 $CO_{2}$ molecules.

The fixation of one $CO_{2}$ molecule in the Calvin cycle consumes 3 ATP and 2 NADPH. Thus, one glucose molecule requires $6 \times 3 = 18$ ATP and $6 \times 2 = 12$ NADPH.

If 72 molecules of ATP are consumed, the number of glucose molecules synthesized is $\dfrac{72}{18} = 4$ molecules.

Since each glucose molecule requires the oxidation of 12 NADPH molecules, the total number of NADPH molecules oxidized is $4 \times 12 = 48$ molecules.

Dividing 72 by 12 (forgetting the 18 ATP per glucose stoichiometry) leads to the incorrect assumption of 6 glucose molecules.

Answer: 4 molecules of glucose and 48 molecules of NADPH

126281.text:

Assertion (A): In plants like castor and maize, autogamy is prevented but not geitonogamy.
Reason (R): In these plants, male and female flowers are borne on the same individual.

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
126281.sol:
Assertion (A) is true. In plants like castor and maize, autogamy (transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower) is prevented, but geitonogamy (transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of another flower of the same plant) can still occur.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A). Castor and maize are monoecious plants, meaning they bear unisexual male and female flowers on the same individual plant. Because the flowers are unisexual, autogamy is impossible. However, since both types of flowers are on the same plant, pollen from a male flower can easily reach the stigma of a female flower on that same plant, allowing geitonogamy.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion

126298.subject: Botany
126298.text: If the meiocyte of a black pepper plant contains $24$ chromosomes, what will be the respective number of chromosomes in the cells of its perisperm and endosperm?
126298.sol:
The meiocyte is a diploid cell ($2n$), so $2n = 24$. This means the haploid chromosome number is $n = 12$.

The perisperm is the persistent remnant of the nucellus. Since the nucellus is a maternal sporophytic tissue, its cells are diploid ($2n$). Therefore, the number of chromosomes in the cells of the perisperm is $24$.

The endosperm in angiosperms develops from the primary endosperm nucleus formed by triple fusion, making it a triploid tissue ($3n$). Therefore, the number of chromosomes in the endosperm is $3 \times 12 = 36$.

Thus, the respective chromosome numbers are $24$ and $36$.

Answer: $24$ and $36$

127872.subject: Zoology
127872.text: What is tissue in multicellular animals?
options: A single cell performing all functions
A group of similar cells performing different functions
A group of similar cells along with intercellular substances performing a specific function
Different groups of cells performing all functions
127872.sol: In the preceding chapters you came across a large variety of organisms, both unicellular and multicellular, of the animal kingdom. In unicellular organisms, all functions like digestion, respiration and reproduction are performed by a single cell. In the complex body of multicellular animals the same basic functions are carried out by different groups of cells in a well organised manner. The body of a simple organism like Hydra is made of different types of cells and the number of cells in each type can be in thousands. The human body is composed of billions of cells to perform various functions. How do these cells in the body work together? As you have already learnt in your earlier classes, in multicellular animals, a group of similar cells alongwith intercellular substances perform a specific function. Such an organisation is called tissue. You may be surprised to know that all complex animals consist of only four basic types of tissues. These tissues are organised in specific proportion and pattern to form an organ like stomach, lung, heart and kidney. When two or more organs perform a common function by their physical and/or chemical interaction, they together form organ system, e.g., digestive system, respiratory system, etc. Cells, tissues, organs and organ systems split up the work in a way that exhibits division of labour and contribute to the survival of the body as a whole.
127872.meta: What is tissue in multicellular animals?

128007.subject: Zoology
128007.text: The stomach of the frog contains
128007.sol: Food is captured by the bilobed tongue. Digestion of food takes place by the action of HCl and gastric juices secreted from the walls of the stomach. Partially digested food called chyme is passed from the stomach to the first part of the intestine, the duodenum. The duodenum receives bile from gallbladder and pancreatic juices from the pancreas through a common bile duct. Bile emulsifies fat and pancreatic juices digest carbohydrates and proteins. Final digestion takes place in the intestine. Digested food is absorbed by the numerous finger-like folds in the inner wall of intestine called villi and microvilli. The undigested solid waste moves into the rectum and passes out through cloaca.

128283.subject: Zoology
128283.text: What is the function of the pars distalis of the pituitary gland?
options: To store and release oxytocin and vasopressin
To produce growth hormone, prolactin, thyroid stimulating hormone, adrenocorticotrophic hormone, luteinizing hormone and follicle stimulating hormone
128283.sol: The pituitary gland is located in a bony cavity called sella tursica and is attached to hypothalamus by a stalk (Figure 19.2). It is divided anatomically into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis. Adenohypophysis consists of two portions, pars distalis and pars intermedia. The pars distalis region of pituitary, commonly called anterior pituitary, produces growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL), thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH), luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH). Pars intermedia secretes only one hormone called melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH). However, in humans, the pars intermedia is almost merged with pars distalis. Neurohypophysis (pars nervosa) also known as posterior pituitary, stores and releases two hormones called oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesised by the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to neurohypophysis.
